narrator.name: Narrator
narrator.note: Reads the lines that introduce each speech.

job.name: Job
job.note: The afflicted just man of Hus, answering his friends and pleading his cause before God.

2.t: How long do you afflict my soul, and break me in pieces with words?

3.t: Behold, these ten times you confound me, and are not ashamed to oppress me.

4.t: For if I have been ignorant, my ignorance shall be with me.

5.t: But you set yourselves up against me, and reprove me with my reproaches.

6.t: At least now understand, that God hath not afflicted me with an equal judgment, and compassed me with his scourges.

7.t: Behold I shall cry suffering violence, and no one will hear: I shall cry aloud, and there is none to judge.

8.t: He hath hedged in my path round about, and I cannot pass, and in my way he hath set darkness.

9.t: He hath stripped me of my glory, and hath taken the crown from my head.

10.t: He hath destroyed me on every side, and I am lost, and he hath taken away my hope, as from a tree that is plucked up.

11.t: His wrath is kindled against me, and he hath counted me as his enemy.

12.t: His troops have come together, and have made themselves a way by me, and have besieged my tabernacle round about.

13.t: He hath put my brethren far from me, and my acquaintance like strangers have departed from me.

14.t: My kinsmen have forsaken me, and they that knew me, have forgotten me.

15.t: They that dwell in my house, and my maidservants have counted me as a stranger, and I have been like an alien in their eyes.

16.t: I called my servant, and he gave me no answer, I entreated him with my own mouth.

17.t: My wife hath abhorred my breath, and I entreated the children of my womb.

18.t: Even fools despised me, and when I was gone from them, they spoke against me.

19.t: They that were sometime my counsellors, have abhorred me: and he whom I loved most is turned against me.

20.t: The flesh being consumed, my bone hath cleaved to my skin, and nothing but lips are left about my teeth.

21.t: Have pity on me, have pity on me, at least you my friends, because the hand of the Lord hath touched me.

22.t: Why do you persecute me as God, and glut yourselves with my flesh?

23.t: Who will grant me that my words may be written? who will grant me that they may be marked down in a book?

24.t: With an iron pen and in a plate of lead, or else be graven with an instrument in flint stone?

25.t: For I know that my Redeemer liveth, and in the last day I shall rise out of the earth.

26.t: And I shall be clothed again with my skin, and in my flesh I shall see my God.

27.t: Whom I myself shall see, and my eyes shall behold, and not another: this my hope is laid up in my bosom.

28.t: Why then do you say now: Let us persecute him, and let us find occasion of word against him?

29.t: Flee then from the face of the sword, for the sword is the revenger of iniquities: and know ye that there is a judgment.
